ranked_facts.why: The presence of a complete right bundle-branch block is more consistent with Ostium Secundum Atrial Septal Defect, as it often presents with right axis deviation and bundle branch block, whereas Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy typically presents with T-wave inversion and epsilon waves.

ranked_facts.concept_key: step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium
ranked_facts.why: The step-up in oxygenation from the superior vena cava to the right atrium is indicative of a left-to-right shunt, which is characteristic of Ostium Secundum Atrial Septal Defect, whereas Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy does not typically present with a significant shunt.

f4a2c3d860c209e9c6b76b7ced349647363f901c.why: The systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region is a common finding in patients with atrial septal defects due to increased flow across the pulmonary valve.

f8a981d23ab00c16f00c81d9359d8243cc0c0ebe.why: The finding of low pulmonary vascular resistance supports Atrial Septal Defect as it is consistent with a left-to-right shunt typically seen in this condition.

ranked_facts.concept_key: no history of dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling
ranked_facts.why: The absence of symptoms such as dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling is more consistent with a condition like Ostium Secundum Atrial Septal Defect (B1), where patients are often asymptomatic, especially in the early stages, than with conditions like Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (B2), which may present with such symptoms due to the progression of the disease affecting the right ventricle's ability to pump blood effectively.

ranked_facts.concept_key: transesophageal echocardiogram confirms the defect
ranked_facts.why: The confirmation of the defect by transesophageal echocardiogram is highly supportive of Ostium Secundum Atrial Septal Defect (B1), as this diagnostic tool can accurately visualize the defect, whereas Conduction Disorder (B3) might not be directly diagnosed or confirmed through this method alone.
